question: How the player puts a finished unit on the map: what opens the list, what a line of it does, and what joining a unit in the field means.

structs.name: CSideMenuDeploy
structs.comment: The side menu that lists a country's finished units, on the `sidebar_deploy` window of interface/sidebar.gui. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-deploymenu.md.
structs.evidence: The constructor at rva 0x4277A0 writes the table at VA 0x15E02F0 after CSideMenu's.

addresses.name: CSideMenuDeploy::CSideMenuDeploy
addresses.comment: Makes the deploy menu: a CDeploymentMenuMouseObserver for the map (0x1C bytes, built inline), CSideMenu's constructor with the window name `sidebar_deploy`, and its own button observer on `close`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-deploymenu.md.
addresses.evidence: The literals 'sidebar_deploy' (0x827801) and 'close'; the table writes 0x15E02F0 and, for the observer, 0x15E02E4. `ret 8`.

addresses.name: CSideMenuDeploy::Update
addresses.comment: **Slot 7, and the whole of the menu's behaviour.** Not choosing a target: when `deployment_queue` holds a different number of lines than the country has deployments, or `list_stale` is set, CSideMenuDeploy_BuildList; and when the list is empty the menu closes itself (CInGameIdler_CloseSideMenus). Choosing a target: once, the list is emptied, the title set to the text of DEPLOY_SEL_TARGET, and a CDeploymentTargetEntry added for each unit of the country - walked by oob_level 0 to 7 and within a level in the country's order - that stands where the deployment may be placed, is not lent out, and: for a new land unit of one brigade, is land with fewer brigades than CCountry_GetMaxBrigadesInDivision; for another new land unit, passes CUnit_MayTakeSubordinate; for a new air unit, is an air unit (with a rule about carrier air groups that was not read through); for a new fleet, is a fleet. No such unit puts the menu back to its plain list. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-deploymenu.md.
addresses.evidence: The literals 'deployment_queue', 'DEPLOY_SEL_TARGET' and 'title_view_deploy'; the loop `for level in 0..7` over CCountry's unit list with `[unit+0x1f4] == level`; the deployment's slot 10 called with the unit's province; `expeditionary_owner.id == 0`; the three `operator_new(0xd0)` before CDeploymentTargetEntry's constructor. Bare `ret`.

addresses.name: CSideMenuDeploy_BuildList
addresses.comment: Sets `title_view_deploy` to the text of DEPLOY_UNITS, empties `deployment_queue` and adds one CDeploymentEntry (0xA8 bytes) for each of the country's deployments (CCountry +0x688), in that list's order. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-deploymenu.md.
addresses.evidence: The three literals; the walk of `countries[tag]->deployments` with `[node+8]` as next; `operator_new(0xa8)` and the constructor at 0x826F40 per node. `ret 4`.

addresses.name: CSideMenuDeploy_ChooseDeployment
addresses.no_signature: the menu in ESI and the deployment on the stack; `ret 4`
addresses.comment: **A unit has been chosen to place**: stores the deployment's id in the menu (+0x5C, +0x60), sets `choosing_target` (+0x58) and `targets_stale` (+0x64), and remembers the list's scroll position (+0x68). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-deploymenu.md.
addresses.evidence: `mov [esi+0x60],[param+0xc]; mov [esi+0x5c],[param+8]; mov byte ptr [esi+0x58],1; mov byte ptr [esi+0x64],1`, then the scrollbar read into +0x68.

addresses.name: CSideMenuDeploy::Show
addresses.comment: Slot 2: shows the window, clears `choosing_target` and `targets_stale`, builds the list.
addresses.evidence: The window's slot 13, two byte clears at +0x58 and +0x64, the call of 0x8287B0.

addresses.name: CSideMenuDeploy::Hide
addresses.comment: Slot 3: hides the window and calls the in-game screen's slot 30 with 0 - no deployment is being placed.
addresses.evidence: The window's slot 14, `push 0` and the call through `[[this+0x20]]+0x78`, the clear of +0x64.

addresses.name: CDeploymentEntry::CDeploymentEntry
addresses.signature: CDeploymentEntry* __stdcall CDeploymentEntry::CDeploymentEntry(CDeploymentEntry* this, void* inGameScreen, CSideMenuDeploy* menu, void* deployment)
addresses.comment: **One finished unit's line**, on a `deployment_entry` window: `name` is the deployment's own name (its slot 11); for a unit's deployment (slot 8 answering 0x4B4) `counter_type` gets the sprite `GFX_counter_<key of the unit's first brigade's type>` where that sprite exists, and `counter_size` the frame CUnit::GetCounterSize + 1, worked out inline; for any other deployment both icons are hidden. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-deploymenu.md.
addresses.evidence: The literals 'deployment_entry', 'select', 'name', 'GFX_counter_', 'counter_type', 'counter_size'; the jump table at 0x827388 with the same seven cases as 0x5BD1C0; the icon's slot 18 with `size + 1`. `ret 0x10`.

addresses.name: CDeploymentEntry::OnSelect
addresses.comment: Slot 4, the `select` button: finds the deployment by its id, resets the menu's mouse observer, tells the in-game screen which deployment is being placed (its slot 30), and for a unit's deployment calls CSideMenuDeploy_ChooseDeployment; for any other kind the in-game screen's slot 46. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-deploymenu.md.
addresses.evidence: FindPersistentById on `[this+0x7c]`,`[this+0x80]`; the call through `+0x78`; the compare of slot 8's answer with 0x4B4.

addresses.name: CDeploymentTargetEntry::CDeploymentTargetEntry
addresses.signature: CDeploymentTargetEntry* __stdcall CDeploymentTargetEntry::CDeploymentTargetEntry(CDeploymentTargetEntry* this, void* inGameScreen, void* list, void* deployment, CUnit* unit)
addresses.comment: **One unit the new one may join**, on a `deployment_target_entry` window: `name` the unit's name (slot 7), `location` the name of the province it is in, `counter_type` and `counter_size` as CDeploymentEntry's, from this unit. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-deploymenu.md.
addresses.evidence: The literals 'deployment_target_entry', 'select', 'name', 'location', 'GFX_counter_'; the jump table at 0x8268D0. `ret 0x14`.

addresses.name: CDeploymentTargetEntry::OnSelect
addresses.comment: Slot 4, the `select` button: posts a CDeployUnitCommand with the target unit's province, the player's tag, the deployment's id and the unit's id as the target, tells the in-game screen no deployment is being placed, and clears the menu's `choosing_target`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-deploymenu.md.
addresses.evidence: `operator_new(0x58)` and CDeployUnitCommand's constructor with `[[unit+0x130]+0xd0]`, the tag pair, `[deployment+8]`,`+0xc` and `[unit+0x10]`,`+0x14`; `mov byte ptr [menu+0x58],0`.

addresses.name: CDeploymentTargetEntry_Refresh
addresses.no_signature: `this` is the object's second base, at +0x1C
addresses.comment: Slot 9 of the line's second table: finds its deployment and its unit again by id, and where the deployment may no longer be placed in the unit's province (the deployment's slot 10) calls CSideMenuDeploy_ChooseDeployment, so the target list is made again.
addresses.evidence: The decompiled C; two FindPersistentById and the slot 10 call.

addresses.name: CDropAndAssignUnitDeploymentCallback::Call
addresses.comment: Slot 0: posts a CDeployUnitCommand for the deployment the callback holds (+4), with the unit it is called with as the target and that unit's province as the place. It is what answers when a deployment's line is dropped on a unit on the map. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-deploymenu.md.
addresses.evidence: `operator_new(0x58)` and CDeployUnitCommand's constructor with `[[unit+0x130]+0xd0]`, `[[this+4]+8]`,`+0xc` and `[unit+0x10]`,`+0x14`. `ret 4`.

addresses.name: CDeploymentMenuMouseObserver::OnMouse
addresses.comment: Slot 1 of the deploy menu's observer of the map. On a left click with a deployment's line under way and the pointer inside the map's rectangle, it finds the unit that deployment holds (0x8274A0), makes a CDropAndAssignUnitDeploymentCallback, and opens the routine that lets a unit be dropped on another - 0x73B280 for a unit of one brigade, 0x73AE80 otherwise. Likely; only its outline was read, and the plain click on a province is not here. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-deploymenu.md.
addresses.evidence: The decompiled C: `[this+0x18] == 1`, the rectangle test, `operator_new(0xc)` with the table 0x15E02DC, `[unit+0x40] == 1` choosing between the two routines. Ghidra labels this address the callback's constructor; the RTTI export has it as the observer's slot 1.

addresses.name: CUnitDeployment::JoinUnit
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CUnitDeployment::JoinUnit(CUnitDeployment* this, CCountry* country, CUnit* target, bool findAnother)
addresses.comment: **Puts a finished unit with one already in the field.** The place is the target's province, or - where the deployment may not be placed there - the nearest province of the capital's area where it may (its ports for a fleet, its air bases for an air unit); none, and nothing happens. The unit is placed (slot 9), the deployment unlinked from the country's list and freed, and then: **a unit of exactly one brigade, of the same service as the target, has that brigade moved into the target** (RemoveRegimentFromUnit, AddRegimentToUnit), a TRANSFEREDSUBUNIT message is raised for the player, and the emptied unit is removed from the game; any other unit is put under the target (0x5B9760). With the flag set the target is first swapped by one of two AI helpers, not read. Called by CDeployUnitCommand::Execute. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-deploymenu.md.
addresses.evidence: The deployment's slot 10 on the target's province; the walk of the area's list with CMap::DistanceBetweenProvinces keeping the least; slot 9; the unlink from `[country+0x688]`; `[unit+0x40] == 1`; the two regiment calls; the literals 'SUB', 'OLD', 'NEW', 'TRANSFEREDSUBUNIT'; CGameState::RemoveUnit. `ret 0xc`. "Of the same service" is likely, not confirmed: the decompiler loses the comparison of the six IsLand/IsAir/IsNaval answers.

addresses.name: CUnit_MayTakeSubordinate
addresses.no_signature: the commander in EAX, the subordinate and a flag on the stack
addresses.comment: **Whether one unit may be put under another.** False unless the commander's oob_level is lower than the subordinate's. For a land subordinate under anything but a theatre (level 0): false where the commander already has more than four land units under it - the limit BiceLib hooks. For a naval or air subordinate: false where the commander's level is above 3. With the flag set the subordinate itself is not counted. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-deploymenu.md.
addresses.evidence: `mov [eax+0x1f4]` against `[param+0x1f4]` with `jle` to false; slots 17 and 16 of the subordinate; the count of the commander's children (+0x1E4) whose slot 15 answers, and `cmp ..,4; jg`; `cmp dword ptr [eax+0x1f4],3; jg`. `ret 8`. The two hook labels the record already has inside it are at the count.

addresses.name: CCountry_GetMaxBrigadesInDivision
addresses.comment: `(BRIGADES_IN_DIVISION + the int at +0x1C of the object at CCountry +0xDF8) / 1000`: how many brigades the country may put in one division.
addresses.evidence: GetDefines, `[defines.military]->BRIGADES_IN_DIVISION`, the add of `[[country+0xdf8]+0x1c]`, the divide by 1000. `ret 4`.

addresses.name: CAlertManager::CAlertManager
addresses.no_signature: the manager is the first of three stack arguments and ECX carries another object
addresses.comment: Makes the alert manager: sixteen alert records of 0x88 bytes, a button observer whose handler is CAlertManager::OnIconClicked, the places `alerticon_startposition`, `alerticon_offset` and `alerticon_mp_offset` read from the interface files, and the sixteen alerts registered by name and number - 0 alert_nap_expiry, 1 alert_deployable_units, 2 alert_troops_in_foreign_territory, 3 alert_revoltrisk_in_provinces, 4 alert_can_invite_to_faction, 5 alert_resource_panic, 6 alert_possible_law, 7 alert_free_tech_slots, 8 alert_wasted_ic, 9 alert_tech_far_ahead, 10 alert_lack_of_troops, 11 alert_bad_supply, 12 alert_national_decisions, 13 alert_mobilized_in_peace, 14 alert_victory_conditions, 15 alert_allied_objectives. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-deploymenu.md.
addresses.evidence: Sixteen literals, each followed by the call of 0x601B70 with its number; the table write CButtonObserverGlue<CAlertManager>. `ret 0xc`.

addresses.name: CAlertManager_Register
addresses.no_signature: the name in ECX, the manager and the number on the stack; `ret 8`
addresses.comment: Records one alert's name and renders its two tooltips, from the localisation keys `<name>_instant` and `<name>_delayed`, into the record `manager + number * 0x88`.
addresses.evidence: The literals '_instant' and '_delayed' appended to the name; two GetText.

addresses.name: CAlertManager_Show
addresses.no_signature: the manager in EDI and the number on the stack; `ret 4`
addresses.comment: **Puts an alert's icon on screen**: makes an `alerticon_window`, sets its `alerticon` to frame `number + 1` and its `alerticon_banner` to frame 0, hooks the icon to the manager's observer, and places the window at the manager's next place (+8, +0xC), which then moves on by `alerticon_offset`'s x (+0x10). Plays the `message` sound. Likely. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-deploymenu.md.
addresses.evidence: The decompiled C: the literals 'alerticon_window', 'alerticon', 'alerticon_banner', 'alert_scope', 'message'; the icon's slot 18 with `number + 1`; `[mgr+8] += [mgr+0x10]`.

addresses.name: CAlertManager::OnIconClicked
addresses.comment: Finds which of the sixteen alerts a clicked icon is - by its frame less one, or by being that alert's banner - and hands the alert's name to the in-game screen's slot 80. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-deploymenu.md.
addresses.evidence: The loop of 0x10 over records of 0x88 bytes; the button's slot 19 less 1 compared with the index; the call through `+0x140` with `record + 0x60`. `ret 4`.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::OnAlertClicked
addresses.comment: **Slot 80: what a click on an alert does**, by the alert's name. It closes the open side menu first. For `alert_deployable_units` it opens side menu 5, the deploy menu (CInGameIdler_OpenSideMenu). Only that arm was read; the function goes on through the other alerts. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-deploymenu.md.
addresses.evidence: The byte-wise compare with the literal 'alert_deployable_units' twice (0x64AD09, 0x64AE64), the second followed by `push 5` and the call of 0x6655C0. `ret 4`.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler_OpenSideMenu
addresses.no_signature: the screen in a register and the number on the stack; `ret 4`
addresses.comment: Opens one of the in-game screen's side menus by number; 5 is the deploy menu. Only its call was read.
addresses.evidence: Called with 5 straight after the test for alert_deployable_units.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler_CloseSideMenus
addresses.comment: Closes every side menu that says it is open (each one's slot 4, then its slot 3) from the vector at CInGameIdler +0xD10, and tidies the selection panel. The deploy menu calls it on itself when its list is empty.
addresses.evidence: The loop over `[eax+0xd10]`..`[eax+0xd14]` calling `+0x10` then `+0xc`.

addresses.name: CInGameIdler::SetDeploymentBeingPlaced
addresses.comment: Slot 30. Called with the deployment when a line of the deploy menu is chosen and with 0 when the menu closes or a target is picked. The name is from those three calls; the body was not read. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-deploymenu.md.
addresses.evidence: The three call sites through `+0x78`: CDeploymentEntry::OnSelect with the deployment, CSideMenuDeploy::Hide with 0, CDeploymentTargetEntry::OnSelect. `ret 4`.
